title: Measuring Money: M1 and M2
short: M1 holds the most liquid forms of money; M2 adds less liquid ones such as small time deposits.
trouble: Students count stocks, bonds or unused credit limits as money, or think M1 and M2 are separate pools rather than M2 containing M1.

blocks.html: Money is whatever is accepted in payment, but some assets are closer to spendable than others. A checking balance can be spent today; a bond must first be sold. The Federal Reserve measures money at two levels of liquidity.

M1 = currency held by the public + checking (demand) deposits + other liquid deposits, which since May 2020 include savings deposits. M2 = M1 + small time deposits (certificates of deposit under \$100,000) + retail money market fund balances. M2 contains M1. Stocks, bonds and credit limits are not money.

Liquidity is how quickly and cheaply something can be spent. Currency and checking deposits are as liquid as it gets. Savings deposits used to be counted only in M2, because withdrawals were limited; in 2020 the Federal Reserve dropped that limit and moved savings deposits into M1. (Older textbooks still put savings in M2 only.) Time deposits and money market funds take a step or a short wait to spend, so they are in M2 but not M1. The measures are nested circles, not separate pools.

blocks.html: How much money there is matters for spending and prices. When the money supply grows much faster than the economy's output for years, prices rise; when it shrinks suddenly, spending can collapse, as in the early 1930s. The central bank watches the money measures, along with interest rates and other data, when it sets policy. Later lessons connect the money supply to interest rates (the money market) and to inflation (the quantity theory).

items: Less liquid: small time deposits and retail money market funds (M2 only).
Not money: stocks, bonds, houses, credit limits.

blocks.html: Counting stocks, bonds or unused credit limits as money, or treating M1 and M2 as separate pools. M2 includes all of M1. Check: when you compute M2, start from M1 and add.
